issues.description: The problem statement contains a conflicting parameter type for addGuestStudents: one place (task description) incorrectly asks for addGuestStudents(String) while the UML diagram and the provided solution expect addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch will confuse students about what parameter type to implement and may cause signature or type errors when comparing against tests or the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the problem statement to consistently specify addGuestStudents(int) as the required method signature (matching the UML diagram and solution). Alternatively, if a String parameter was intended, update the UML diagram and solution to use String and clarify how the string should be interpreted. The preferred fix is to change the task description line to: "Implement an addGuestStudents(int) method which adds a new number of guest students to the lecture."

issues.description: The problem statement text instructs implementing addGuestStudents(String) (textual task), but the UML and the solution implementation use addGuestStudents(int). This mismatched parameter type (String vs int) for the same conceptual method can confuse students about the expected signature and return type, leading to incorrect implementations or wasted time trying to reconcile the discrepancy.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement with the UML and implementation by changing the task text to require addGuestStudents(int) (i.e., accept an int parameter for the number of new guest students). Alternatively, if a String is intended, update the UML and solution to use addGuestStudents(String) consistently. The simplest fix is to update problem_statement.md to specify addGuestStudents(int).
